orders.title: 2-up at range, HANDHELD: a42q | a42k (13 ft, 5× optical) — the streams' first handheld take
orders.why: The continuous receiver's per-emitter beacon streams accumulate a rolling 60-s phase track per tile and stitch window seams by whole turns; every twin is tripod-still. A handheld take at range prices that 60-s span against real clock wander and hand sway — the referee named on the phase-B record. Keep 5× OPTICAL (10× is software past 5× and kills the beacon); handheld, no rest. The receiver runs at default windows now — no minwin/maxwin needed.

orders.title: The first LIVE take: a42q, close (5×/5 ft, tripod) — the receiver on the camera, no clip
orders.why: Phase C put live capture behind the same source interface as recordings; the synthetic live twin certified the path on a wall clock, but no photon has crossed the ring buffer yet. This take prices the buffer's memory budget (640-px luma, 30-s retention) and the dead-air guard on a real phone. THE FLOW DIFFERS: arm the emitter from this card as usual; on the receiver page (on the phone or a laptop with a camera) paste the same settings, Start camera, frame the plate, then LIVE HARVEST — not Capture, not a clip file. The harvest posts its own log (clip 'camera-live', source live); Stop live when it reports the peel (or after ~60 s if it does not — that is evidence too).
